Subject: Long-context eval discussion

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo earlier today — great overview. As discussed on the call, our main risk areas for this project are:
- Model quality on large meeting transcripts (we routinely hit 15-25k token meetings)
- Truncation behavior and whether summaries lose critical context
- Regression vs our current baseline (we run an internal fine-tuned model)

Can you send a post-call recap with recommended Redwood models to try, the benchmark links you mentioned, and a sample prompt set we can run? Procurement will also want a mutual action plan and a simple evaluation plan to review.

I'll attach a typical long meeting transcript (20k tokens) in a follow-up so you can reproduce locally.

Thanks,
Sofia Lopez
Product Manager, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Long-context eval discussion

Hi Sofia — great to meet you earlier, and thanks for the clear list of risk areas. Quick recap + next steps below.

Recap of call (short):
- Primary goal: reliable, concise meeting summaries and action item extraction from 15-25k token transcripts.
- Success criteria: per-meeting summarization fidelity >= 0.88 (ROUGE/ROUGE-L vs human), and no critical-item drop (manual check).
- Constraints: latency target for real-time-ish summaries is ~2-3s per 1k tokens for live pipeline; batch summarization can be slower.

Recommended Redwood models to evaluate (initial sweep):
- redwood-large-32k: best candidate for fidelity with long context windows (32k).
- rw-medium-16k-quant: cost-efficient option, supports up to 16k; we expect some context degradation >16k but worth quantizing for cost tests.
- redwood-fallback-8k: for latency-sensitive routes and comparison to your current baseline.

Benchmarks / resources (internal links):
- Long-context eval guide: https://redwood.app/drive/long-context-eval
- Public benchmark: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/long_context_summary (contains evaluation harness & metrics)
- Prompt set (attached): acme-long-context-prompt-set.txt — contains extractive + abstractive templates and QA checks.

Attachments included: mutual-action-plan-acme.pdf (MAP), acme-long-context-prompt-set.txt (prompt templates).

Proposed next steps:
1) You to confirm procurement items (MAP) and share a representative transcript file (you mentioned ~20k tokens).
2) Redwood to run a 3-model eval on that transcript + a small set of 10 representative meetings. We'll produce ROUGE/chrF/QA-based precision metrics and a short qualitative report.
3) Follow-up call w/ results and recommended config (expected T+3 business days after we receive transcripts).

Dev/Dylan — can you pick this up? If we can get an initial run in 72 hours after Sofia sends the transcript that should be fine.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Fwd: Long-context eval discussion — action items

Folks — forwarding Sofia's transcript and procurement rubric (attached). Summary of asks and where I'd like us to move quickly:

Ask summary from Acme:
- Run 3-model sweep (redwood-large-32k, rw-medium-16k-quant, redwood-fallback-8k) across the 20k transcript and 9 additional meetings (they'll share 10 total).
- Provide ROUGE-L, ROUGE-1, chrF, and an "action-item recall" metric (binary recall on a hand-labeled set).
- Document truncation behavior and describe approach taken (chunk-and-stitch vs single 32k context).
- Provide a short note on retention: for the eval we should state we won't persist transcripts in hosted logs and that eval data can be processed in a private Dedicated pool if they prefer.

Technical plan (initial):
- Use redwood-large-32k for single-pass where possible. For the 16k quant model, run chunking with overlap (sliding window) + deduped action-item extraction. We'll log token counts and dropped context incidents.
- For summarization fidelity, compute ROUGE metrics vs human summaries and then run an action-item extraction QA (precision/recall) against Acme's labels. Add a short qualitative review for items flagged as missing.

Who does what:
- Dev: set up the eval harness and run the three-model sweep; output metrics CSVs and short qual notes.
- Dylan: sanity-check the prompts and implement overlap/chunking logic to minimize dropped items.

Timeline: initial run within 72 hours after Sofia uploads the full set (target Wed EOD). Short report to Acme and MAP update by next Thu.

Sofia — we'll call out the data retention statement in the MAP. For now, we'll treat these transcripts as non-persistent for hosted evals; offer Dedicated processing if they need guaranteed isolation.

I'll own the customer comms and the MAP update. Let me know if anything looks unrealistic.

Thanks,
Marissa
